_comment: INVERTED POSTURE - this repo is a long-lived FORK, so the house default is
backwards here: dependency management is OFF for everything that came from
upstream, and ON only for what WE added.
WHY. We do not own upstream's dependency tree. Bumping a transitive dep in
packages/*/package.json diverges us from hyperdxio/hyperdx for a fix we did
not write, turns a pristine file into permanent rerere conflict surface
(see FORK.md), and gets reverted or re-conflicted on the next sync anyway.
Upstream patches upstream; we get the fix when we sync. A PR queue full of
bumps we must close unmerged is worse than no queue - it trains everyone to
ignore the queue, including the one bump that matters.
WHAT IS STILL ON. The GitHub Actions pinned by SHA in OUR OWN workflows.
Those are ours, the house standard requires them SHA-pinned, and a stale
pin is a real risk nobody upstream will ever fix for us.
NOT A SUBSTITUTE FOR LOOKING. Muting the per-PR noise does not make an
inherited CVE unreal - the fork ships as a container image. The image scan
at publish is what catches those, and a critical one is an argument for
syncing upstream NOW, not for patching a vendored dep by hand.

packageRules.description: ON: action pins in the workflows we own. Upstream's own workflows are excluded by name, so a sync that adds one does not silently opt it in.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security PRs follow the same rule - our files only. An upstream CVE is fixed by syncing upstream, not by us editing their lockfile.
